rows.stem: A single gene that controls the expression of more than one trait is said to show
rows.solution: When a single gene produces more than one phenotypic effect, it is said to show **pleiotropy** (pleiotropism). Such a gene usually acts through its effect on a metabolic pathway that contributes to several phenotypes; phenylketonuria is the standard example, where one mutant gene causes mental retardation and a reduction in hair and skin pigmentation. Multiple allelism is the presence of more than two alleles of a gene (ABO blood groups), polygenic inheritance is a single trait controlled by three or more genes (human skin colour), and in incomplete dominance the \(\text{F}_1\) shows an intermediate phenotype. So the answer is option (D) Pleiotropism.

rows.stem:
A person with trisomy of 21\(^{\text{st}}\) chromosome shows
(i) Furrowed tongue
(ii) Characteristic palm crease
(iii) Rudimentary ovaries
(iv) Gynaecomastia
Select the correct option, from the choices given below :
rows.solution: Trisomy of chromosome 21 causes **Down's syndrome**. The affected individual is short statured with a small round head, a **furrowed tongue** and a partially open mouth; the palm is broad with the **characteristic palm crease**, and physical, psychomotor and mental development is retarded. Rudimentary ovaries are a feature of Turner's syndrome (44 + XO), and gynaecomastia (development of breasts) of Klinefelter's syndrome (44 + XXY). So the answer is option (D) (i) and (ii).

rows.stem:
Observe the schematic representation of assisted reproductive technology given below :
Identify the most appropriate technique depicted in the above diagram.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a labelled schematic of an assisted reproductive technique: a holding tool, the egg, a needle and a caption saying what the needle does; that caption names the step that identifies the technique, so it is withheld here. Page idx 4.
rows.solution: The diagram shows an egg held steady by a holding tool while a sperm is injected directly into its cytoplasm with a fine needle. This is **intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)**, a specialised procedure in which an embryo is formed in the laboratory by injecting a sperm directly into the ovum. The other choices are different procedures: in IUT an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus, in IUI semen is introduced artificially into the uterus, and in ZIFT a zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube. So the answer is option (C) ICSI.

rows.stem: Interferons are proteins secreted by
rows.solution: Virus-infected cells secrete proteins called **interferons**, which protect the non-infected cells from further viral infection. They form the cytokine barrier, part of innate immunity. So the answer is option (D) Virus infected cell.

rows.stem: During biological treatment of sewage, the masses of bacteria held together by fungal filaments to form mesh like structures are called
rows.solution: In secondary (biological) treatment, the primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks where it is constantly agitated and air is pumped in. This allows vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into **flocs**: masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh like structures. Once the BOD has fallen, the effluent goes to a settling tank where the bacterial flocs sediment; that sediment is the activated sludge, so the term asked for here is the flocs themselves. So the answer is option (B) flocs.

rows.stem: Which one of the following statements is correct in the context of observing DNA separation by agarose gel electrophoresis ?

options.label: A
options.text: DNA can be seen in visible light.

options.label: B
options.text: DNA can be seen without staining in visible light.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethidium bromide stained DNA can be seen in visible light

options.label: D
options.text: Ethidium bromide stained DNA can be seen under UV light.

rows.solution: DNA is not visible in visible light, stained or unstained. After agarose gel electrophoresis the separated fragments are visualised only after staining the DNA with **ethidium bromide** followed by exposure to **UV radiation**, when they show up as bright orange coloured bands. So the answer is option (D) Ethidium bromide stained DNA can be seen under UV light.

rows.stem: A phenomenon where a male insect mistakenly identified the patterns of a orchid flower as the female insect partner, and tries to copulate and thereby pollinates the flower is said to be :
rows.solution: In the Mediterranean orchid Ophrys, one petal bears an uncanny resemblance to the female of a bee species in size, colour and markings. The male bee is attracted to what it perceives as a female and tries to mate with the flower; this is **pseudocopulation**. During it the bee is dusted with pollen, which it carries to another flower, so pollination is achieved. So the answer is option (A) Pseudocopulation.

rows.stem: Identify the correct labellings in the figure of a fertilised embryo sac of an angiosperm given below :

options.label: A
options.text: A – zygote, B – degenerating synergids, C – degenerating antipodals, D – PEN

options.label: B
options.text: A – degenerating synergids, B – zygote, C – PEN, D – degenerating antipodals

options.label: C
options.text: A – degenerating antipodals, B – PEN, C – degenerating synergids, D – zygote

options.label: D
options.text: A – degenerating synergids, B – zygote, C – degenerating antipodals, D – PEN

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a fertilised embryo sac with four pointer labels A, B, C and D and one printed label; which structure each letter points at IS the answer, so it is withheld here. Page idx 6.

rows.stem: Study the pedigree chart of a family showing the inheritance pattern of a certain disorder. Select the option that correctly identifies the nature of the trait depicted in the pedigree chart.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a three-generation pedigree chart of squares and circles, some shaded; which individuals are affected and who their parents are decides the mode of inheritance, so it is withheld here. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
In the first generation both parents are unaffected, yet one son and one daughter are affected, so the trait is **recessive** and both parents must be carriers.
- It cannot be dominant: a dominant trait cannot appear in a child unless one parent shows it.
- It cannot be X-linked recessive: an affected daughter would need an affected father, since she receives one of her X chromosomes from him, and her father is unaffected.

The third generation fits the same pattern: an unaffected couple has an affected son, which is possible when both are carriers. So the answer is option (D) Autosomal recessive.

rows.stem:
Match the following genes of the lac operon listed in column 'A' with their respective products listed in column 'B' :
| A Gene | B Products |
|---|---|
| a. 'i' gene | (i) \(\beta\)-galactosidase |
| b. 'z' gene | (ii) lac permease |
| c. 'a' gene | (iii) repressor |
| d. 'y' gene | (iv) transacetylase |
Select the correct option :
If both the parents are carriers for thalassaemia, the chances of an afflicted child to be born to them is :
rows.solution: Thalassaemia is an autosomal recessive blood disease, so a carrier is heterozygous. Writing the normal allele as T and the thalassaemia allele as t, carrier parents are Tt \(\times\) Tt, which gives offspring in the ratio 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt. Only the tt child is afflicted, so the chance is 1 in 4, that is 25%. So the answer is option (A) 25%.

rows.stem: If the sequence of nitrogen bases of the coding strand in a transcription unit is 5' – ATGAATG – 3', the sequence of bases in its RNA transcript would be
rows.solution: The RNA transcript has the same sequence as the coding strand, with the same polarity (5' to 3'), except that thymine is replaced by uracil. The coding strand 5' – ATGAATG – 3' therefore gives the transcript 5' – AUGAAUG – 3'. (It is the template strand, 3'-TACTTAC-5', that is actually copied.) So the answer is option (A) 5' – AUGAAUG – 3'.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : AIDS is a syndrome caused by HIV.
Reason (R) : HIV is a virus that damages the immune system with DNA as its genetic material.
rows.context: Question number 13 to 16 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution: The Assertion is true: AIDS (Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome) is a syndrome, a set of symptoms caused by the human immuno deficiency virus (HIV). The Reason is false: HIV does damage the immune system (it destroys helper T lymphocytes), but it is a retrovirus whose genetic material is **RNA**, not DNA; its RNA genome is copied into viral DNA by reverse transcriptase inside the host cell. So the Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : In molecular diagnosis, single stranded DNA or RNA tagged with radioactive molecule is called a probe.
Reason (R) : A probe always searches and hybridises with its complementary DNA in a clone of cells.
rows.context: Question number 13 to 16 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution: The Assertion is true: in molecular diagnosis, a **probe** is a single stranded DNA or RNA tagged with a radioactive molecule. The Reason is also true and explains it: such a strand is used as a probe because it searches out and hybridises with its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, after which the clone is detected by autoradiography. A clone with a mutated gene does not appear on the photographic film, because the probe finds no complementarity with it. So both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : In birds the sex of the offspring is determined by males.
Reason (R) : Males are homogametic while females are heterogametic.
rows.context: Question number 13 to 16 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution: The Assertion is false: in birds the sex of the offspring is determined by the **female**, not the male. The Reason is true: females are heterogametic (ZW) and produce two kinds of ova, one carrying Z and the other W, while males are homogametic (ZZ) and produce only one kind of sperm. Which ovum is fertilised decides the sex, so it is the female that decides it. So the Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Communities that comprise of more species tend to be more stable.
Reason (R) : A higher number of species results in less year to year variation in total biomass.
rows.context: Question number 13 to 16 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution: The Assertion is true: communities with more species generally tend to be more stable than those with fewer species. A stable community does not show too much variation in productivity from year to year. The Reason is true and is the explanation: David Tilman's long-term ecosystem experiments found that plots with more species showed **less year-to-year variation in total biomass**, which is exactly what stability means here. So both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem: "Farmers prefer apomictic seeds to hybrid seeds." Justify giving two reasons.
rows.solution:
Any two reasons:
- Hybrid seeds have to be produced **every year**: if the seeds collected from hybrids are sown, the plants in the progeny segregate and do not maintain the hybrid characters.
- Production of hybrid seed is **costly**, so hybrid seeds are expensive for the farmer, while apomictic seeds would be cheaper.
- If hybrids are made into apomicts, there is **no segregation of characters** in the hybrid progeny: apomictic seeds are formed without fertilisation, so they retain the desirable characters of the parent and the farmer can keep using them to raise a new crop year after year.

rows.stem: Mention one advantage and one disadvantage of amniocentesis.
rows.solution:
- **Advantage:** amniocentesis (testing cells from the amniotic fluid) is used to diagnose chromosomal abnormalities or genetic disorders in the foetus, such as Down's syndrome, haemophilia or sickle-cell anaemia, and to judge the survivability of the foetus.
- **Disadvantage:** it can be misused to determine the sex of the foetus, which may lead to female foeticide. For this reason there is a statutory ban on using amniocentesis for sex determination.

rows.stem:
5' – G \(\downarrow\) A A T T C – 3'
3' – C T T A A \(\uparrow\) G – 5'
(a) Name the restriction enzyme that recognises the given specific sequence of bases. What are such sequence of bases referred to as ?
(b) What are the arrows in the given figure indicating ? Write the result obtained thereafter.
rows.solution:
(a) The enzyme is **EcoRI**, which recognises the sequence 5'-GAATTC-3'. Such a sequence is called a **palindromic nucleotide sequence**: it reads the same on the two strands when the orientation of reading is kept the same (5' to 3').

(b) The arrows mark the **restriction sites**, the points where EcoRI cuts each strand of the DNA, between G and A on both strands. Because the cuts are a little away from the centre of the palindrome, the DNA is cut in a staggered way, and each fragment is left with a single-stranded overhanging stretch (AATT) at its end. These overhangs are called **sticky ends**, because they form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts; DNA ligase can then join such fragments, which is what makes recombinant DNA possible.

rows.stem:
Observe the population growth curve and answer the questions given below :
(a) State the conditions under which growth curve 'A' and growth curve 'B' plotted in the graph are possible.
(b) Mention what does 'K' in the graph represent.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a graph of population density (N) against time (t) with two curves labelled A and B, each beside a growth equation, and a dashed horizontal line marked K; which curve carries which equation and shape decides part (a), so that is withheld here. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
(a)
- Curve 'A' is the J-shaped exponential growth curve, \(\frac{dN}{dt} = rN\). It is possible when resources (food and space) are **unlimited**, so there is no competition or environmental resistance to check growth.
- Curve 'B' is the sigmoid logistic growth curve, \(\frac{dN}{dt} = rN\left(\frac{K - N}{K}\right)\). It is possible when resources are **limited**, so competition and environmental resistance slow growth until the population levels off.

(b) 'K' is the **carrying capacity**: the maximum number of individuals of a population that a given habitat can support, beyond which no further growth is possible.

rows.stem: Explain how are plants benefitted by their association with "Glomus species".
If the base adenine constitutes 31% of an isolated DNA fragment, then write what will be the expected percentage of the base cytosine in it. Explain how did you arrive at the answer given.
rows.solution:
The expected percentage of cytosine is **19%**.

By Chargaff's rule, in double stranded DNA the amount of adenine equals that of thymine and the amount of guanine equals that of cytosine, because A pairs with T and G pairs with C (the ratios A/T and G/C are each 1).
- Adenine is 31%, so thymine is also 31%, and \(\text{A} + \text{T} = 62\%\).
- The rest is guanine and cytosine: \(\text{G} + \text{C} = 100\% - 62\% = 38\%\).
- G and C are equal, so cytosine is \(38\% \div 2 = 19\%\).

rows.stem:
Identify a, b, c, d, e and f in the table given below :
| Sl. No. | Organism | Bioactive Molecule | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Monascus purpureus | a | b |
| 2. | c | d | Antibiotic |
| 3. | e | Cyclosporin A | f |
rows.solution:
| Sl. No. | Organism | Bioactive Molecule | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Monascus purpureus | **a**: Statins | **b**: blood-cholesterol lowering agent |
| 2. | **c**: Penicillium notatum | **d**: Penicillin | Antibiotic |
| 3. | **e**: Trichoderma polysporum | Cyclosporin A | **f**: immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients |

Statins, produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus, lower blood cholesterol by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis. For c and d the marking scheme accepts any other correct pair of an organism and the antibiotic it produces.

rows.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
rows.stem: Tropical regions harbour more species than the temperate regions. How have biologists tried to explain this in their own ways ? Explain.
rows.solution:
Ecologists have proposed three explanations for the greater diversity of the tropics:
- **Long evolutionary time:** speciation is generally a function of time. Temperate regions were subjected to frequent glaciations in the past, whereas tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years and so have had a long evolutionary time for species diversification.
- **Constant environment:** tropical environments, unlike temperate ones, are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable. Such constant environments promote niche specialisation and lead to greater species diversity.
- **More solar energy:** more solar energy is available in the tropics, which contributes to higher productivity; this in turn might contribute indirectly to greater diversity.

rows.stem:
(i) What does an ecological pyramid represent ?
(ii) The Ecological pyramids may have an 'upright' or an 'inverted' shape. Justify with the help of suitable examples.
rows.solution:
(i) An **ecological pyramid** is a diagrammatic representation of the relationship between organisms at different trophic levels, expressed in terms of number, biomass or energy. The base is always the producers (first trophic level) and the apex the top level consumers.

(ii)
- **Upright pyramid:** the number, biomass or energy is greater at the producer level than at the consumer levels. Example: the pyramid of numbers or of biomass in a grassland ecosystem, drawn as a broad bar for producers with narrower bars for primary, secondary and tertiary consumers above it. The pyramid of energy is always upright.
- **Inverted pyramid:** the number or biomass is smaller at the producer level than at the consumer level. Examples: the pyramid of biomass in the sea, where a small standing crop of phytoplankton supports a large standing crop of zooplankton; and the pyramid of numbers of a single big tree supporting a large number of insects. Drawn, the narrow producer bar sits at the bottom under a wider consumer bar.

rows.stem:
(a) What are transgenic animals ?
(b) Name the transgenic animal having the largest number amongst all the existing transgenic animals.
(c) State any 3 reasons for which these types of animals are being produced.

If the cells in the leaves of a maize plant contain 10 chromosomes each, write the number of chromosomes in its endosperm and zygote. Name and explain the process by which an endosperm and a zygote are formed in maize.
rows.solution:
The leaf cells are diploid, so \(2n = 10\) and \(n = 5\).
- **Endosperm: 15 chromosomes** (triploid, \(3n\)).
- **Zygote: 10 chromosomes** (diploid, \(2n\)).

Both form by **double fertilisation** inside the embryo sac, after the pollen tube releases two male gametes:
- One male gamete fuses with the egg cell. This is **syngamy**, and it forms the diploid zygote (\(n + n = 2n\)).
- The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei in the central cell. This involves three haploid nuclei and is called **triple fusion**; it forms the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (\(n + n + n = 3n\)), which develops into the endosperm.

Since two kinds of fusion take place in one embryo sac, the event is called double fertilisation.

rows.stem:
(a) Why does DNA replication occur within a replication fork and not in its entire length simultaneously ?
(b) "DNA replication is continuous and discontinuous on the two strands within the replication fork." Explain with the help of a schematic representation.
rows.solution:
(a) Replication is an energetically very expensive process (the deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates serve both as substrates and as the energy source). For long DNA molecules the two strands cannot be separated along their entire length at once because of this very high energy requirement, so replication proceeds within a small opening of the helix, the **replication fork**.

(b) The DNA-dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in only one direction, **5' to 3'**. So within the fork:
- on the template strand with polarity **3' to 5'**, the new strand is made **continuously**;
- on the template strand with polarity **5' to 3'**, it is made **discontinuously** as short fragments, which are later joined by the enzyme DNA ligase.

The schematic representation is a Y-shaped fork: the two parental (template) strands are drawn separating, with their 5' and 3' ends marked; one newly synthesised strand runs continuously towards the fork alongside its template, and the other is drawn as a series of short arrows pointing away from the fork, each running 5' to 3'. The marking scheme gives no marks for the diagram if the polarity of the strands is not shown correctly.

rows.stem: Explain the processing of heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA) into a fully functional mRNA in eukaryotes. Where does this processing occur in the cell ?
rows.solution:
In eukaryotes the primary transcript, hnRNA, contains both exons and introns and is non-functional. It is processed into mRNA in three steps:
- **Splicing:** the introns (non-coding sequences) are removed and the exons (coding sequences) are joined together in a defined order.
- **Capping:** an unusual nucleotide, methyl guanosine triphosphate (mGppp), is added to the 5' end of the hnRNA.
- **Tailing:** adenylate residues (200-300) are added at the 3' end in a template-independent manner, forming the poly-A tail.

The fully processed hnRNA is now called mRNA and is transported out of the nucleus for translation.

This processing takes place in the **nucleus**.

rows.stem: The world is facing accelerated rates of species extinction largely due to human activities. Explain any three human activities responsible for accelerated rates of species extinction.
rows.solution:
Any three of these, each with its explanation:
- **Habitat loss and fragmentation:** the most important cause. Tropical rain forests once covered 14% of the earth's land surface and now cover no more than 6%; the Amazon rain forest is being cut and cleared to grow soya beans or to make grassland for beef cattle. When large habitats are broken into small fragments, animals that need large territories, and migratory species, are badly affected and their populations decline.
- **Over-exploitation:** when need turns to greed, natural resources are over-exploited. Many species extinctions in the last 500 years, such as Steller's sea cow and the passenger pigeon, were due to over-exploitation by humans, and many marine fish populations are over-harvested.
- **Alien species invasions:** introduced species can become invasive and cause the decline or extinction of indigenous species. The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in east Africa led eventually to the extinction of more than 200 species of cichlid fish; carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana and water hyacinth (Eicchornia) threaten native species, and the illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture threatens indigenous catfishes.
- **Co-extinctions:** when a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it in an obligatory way also become extinct, for example the parasites of a host fish, or a plant and its specific pollinator in a co-evolved mutualism.

rows.stem: Name the hormones and their source organ, which are responsible for menstrual cycle at puberty.
rows.context: In a human female, the reproductive phase starts on the onset of puberty and ceases around middle age of the female. Study the graph given below regarding menstrual cycle and answer the questions that follow :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE:the menstrual-cycle chart: pituitary hormone levels (FSH, LH), ovarian events (developing follicle to regressing corpus luteum), ovarian hormone levels (estrogen, progesterone) and uterine events against days 1 to 29, with the menstruation, follicular (proliferative) and luteal (secretory) phases named; the sub-part is answerable from text, but the context refers to the graph. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
The menstrual cycle at puberty is controlled by these hormones (any two, with their source):

| Hormone | Source organ |
|---|---|
| FSH (follicle stimulating hormone) | anterior pituitary gland |
| LH (luteinising hormone) | anterior pituitary gland |
| Estrogen | ovary (growing Graafian follicles) |
| Progesterone | ovary (corpus luteum) |

rows.stem: For successful pregnancy, at what phase of the menstrual cycle an early embryo (upto 3 blastomeres) should be Implanted in the Uterus (IUT) of a human female who has opted for Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) ? Support your answer with a reason.
rows.context: In a human female, the reproductive phase starts on the onset of puberty and ceases around middle age of the female. Study the graph given below regarding menstrual cycle and answer the questions that follow :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE:the case study's menstrual-cycle chart, attached so the context's 'graph given below' is not left dangling. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
The embryo should be implanted during the **luteal (secretory) phase**. In this phase the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle form the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone. Progesterone keeps the endometrium thick and well supplied, which is essential for the implantation of the embryo and the other events of pregnancy.

(As printed, the stem calls an embryo of up to 3 blastomeres an IUT case. NCERT transfers embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus (IUT) and earlier embryos, up to 8 blastomeres, into the fallopian tube (ZIFT). The phase in which the uterus is ready to receive an embryo is the luteal phase either way.)

rows.stem: Name the hormone and its source organ responsible for the events occurring during proliferative phase of menstrual cycle. Explain the event.
rows.context: In a human female, the reproductive phase starts on the onset of puberty and ceases around middle age of the female. Study the graph given below regarding menstrual cycle and answer the questions that follow :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE:the case study's menstrual-cycle chart, attached so the context's 'graph given below' is not left dangling. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
The hormone is **estrogen**, secreted by the **ovary** (the growing Graafian follicles), under the stimulation of FSH and LH from the pituitary.

The event: in the proliferative (follicular) phase, the primary follicles in the ovary grow into a fully mature Graafian follicle and, at the same time, the **endometrium of the uterus regenerates through proliferation** after the menstrual flow, becoming thick again in preparation for a possible pregnancy.

rows.stem: In a normal human female, why does menstruation only occurs if the released ovum is not fertilised ? Explain.
rows.context: In a human female, the reproductive phase starts on the onset of puberty and ceases around middle age of the female. Study the graph given below regarding menstrual cycle and answer the questions that follow :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE:the case study's menstrual-cycle chart, attached so the context's 'graph given below' is not left dangling. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
After ovulation, the ruptured follicle forms the **corpus luteum**, which secretes progesterone, and progesterone maintains the thick endometrium.
- If the ovum is **not fertilised**, the corpus luteum degenerates and the progesterone level falls.
- Without progesterone the endometrium cannot be maintained, so it disintegrates together with its blood vessels, and this comes out as the menstrual flow; a new cycle then begins.
- If the ovum **is** fertilised, the corpus luteum is maintained, progesterone keeps the endometrium intact for implantation, and menstruation does not occur.

So menstruation follows only when the released ovum is not fertilised.

rows.stem: Name the form in which Plasmodium gains entry into (i) human body (ii) the female Anopheles body.
rows.context:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow :
"Mosquitoes are drastically affecting the human health in almost all the developing tropical countries. Different species of mosquitoes cause very fatal diseases so much so that many humans loose their life and if they survive, are unable to put in productive hours to sustain their life. With the result the health index of the country goes down."
rows.solution:
(i) Plasmodium enters the human body as **sporozoites** (the infectious form), through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

(ii) It enters the female Anopheles body as **gametocytes** (male and female), taken up with the blood of an infected person.

rows.stem: Why do the symptoms of malaria not appear in a person immediately after being bitten by an infected female Anopheles ? Give one reason. Explain when and how do the symptoms of the disease would appear.
rows.context:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow :
"Mosquitoes are drastically affecting the human health in almost all the developing tropical countries. Different species of mosquitoes cause very fatal diseases so much so that many humans loose their life and if they survive, are unable to put in productive hours to sustain their life. With the result the health index of the country goes down."
rows.solution:
The symptoms do not appear at once because the sporozoites that enter the body must first **multiply asexually**, initially in the liver cells and then inside the red blood cells (RBCs). This takes time.

The symptoms appear when the infected RBCs **rupture**. Their bursting releases a toxic substance, **haemozoin**, which is responsible for the chill and high fever recurring every three to four days.

rows.stem: Explain the events which occur within a female Anopheles mosquito after it has sucked blood from a malaria patient.
rows.context:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow :
"Mosquitoes are drastically affecting the human health in almost all the developing tropical countries. Different species of mosquitoes cause very fatal diseases so much so that many humans loose their life and if they survive, are unable to put in productive hours to sustain their life. With the result the health index of the country goes down."
rows.solution:
- The female Anopheles takes up the **gametocytes** (male and female) with the blood meal from a malaria patient.
- In the mosquito's stomach (gut), the gametes are formed and **fertilisation** takes place.
- The parasites develop further in the gut wall and form **sporozoites**.
- The sporozoites escape from the gut and migrate to the mosquito's **salivary glands**, from where they are injected into a human when the mosquito bites.

rows.stem: Name a species of mosquito other than female Anopheles and the disease, for which it carries the pathogen.
rows.context:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow :
"Mosquitoes are drastically affecting the human health in almost all the developing tropical countries. Different species of mosquitoes cause very fatal diseases so much so that many humans loose their life and if they survive, are unable to put in productive hours to sustain their life. With the result the health index of the country goes down."
rows.solution:
Any one of these:
- **Aedes** mosquito carries the pathogens of **dengue** and **chikungunya**.
- **Culex** mosquito carries the filarial worm Wuchereria, which causes **filariasis (elephantiasis)**.

(i) Name the nematode (scientific name) that infects the roots of tobacco plant and reduces its yield.
(ii) Name the vector that is used to introduce nematode-specific genes into the host plant (tobacco).
(iii) How do sense and anti-sense RNAs function ?
(iv) Why could parasite not survive in a transgenic tobacco plant ?
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: the printed name is spelt "Meloidegyne incognitia"; the nematode is Meloidogyne incognita.]

(i) **Meloidogyne incognita**, a nematode that infects the roots of tobacco plants and causes a great reduction in yield.

(ii) **Agrobacterium tumefaciens** (its Ti plasmid) is used as the vector to introduce the nematode-specific genes into the host plant.

(iii) The nematode-specific genes are introduced so that the host produces both **sense and anti-sense RNA**. The two RNAs are complementary to each other, so they pair to form a **double stranded RNA (dsRNA)**, which initiates RNA interference (RNAi).

(iv) The dsRNA binds to and silences the specific mRNA of the nematode, so that mRNA is **not translated**. The parasite cannot make the protein it needs and could not survive in a transgenic host expressing this specific interfering RNA, so the transgenic plant is protected from the parasite.

rows.stem:
(i) Draw a diagram of a human sperm. Label any four parts and write their functions.
(ii) In a human female, probability of an ovum to get fertilized by more than one sperm is impossible. Give reason.
rows.solution:
(i) A human sperm is drawn with a head, neck, middle piece and tail, enclosed in a plasma membrane. Any four labels with their functions:
- **Head / nucleus:** contains the haploid chromosomal (genetic) material.
- **Acrosome:** a cap-like structure at the tip of the head, filled with enzymes that help in the fertilisation of the ovum.
- **Middle piece:** possesses numerous **mitochondria**, which produce the energy for the movement of the tail.
- **Tail:** gives the sperm motility, which is essential for fertilisation.
- **Plasma membrane:** envelops the whole body of the sperm and protects it.

(ii) During fertilisation, when a sperm comes in contact with the **zona pellucida** layer of the ovum, it induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms. This ensures that only one sperm can fertilise an ovum.

Natural selection operates in different ways in nature.
(i) Identify the type of natural selection depicted in the graph above.
(ii) In England after industrialisation, the population of dark winged moths were more favoured than white winged moth. Explain.
(iii) Anthropogenic action can enhance the rate of evolution. Explain with the help of an example.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a graph of number of individuals against phenotype/trait with two bell curves labelled White Winged moth and Dark Winged moth; how the two curves sit relative to each other decides the type of selection asked in (i), so it is withheld here. Page idx 22.
rows.solution:
(i) **Directional selection.** The graph shows the population's distribution shifting from the original mean towards one extreme (the dark winged moths), which is what happens when one extreme of a trait is favoured.

(ii) This is **industrial melanism**:
- Before industrialisation, tree trunks were covered by white lichens, so white winged moths were camouflaged and survived, while dark winged moths were easily picked out by predators.
- After industrialisation, smoke and soot darkened the tree trunks and lichens could not grow (they do not grow in polluted areas).
- Now the white winged moths were conspicuous and were eaten by predators, while the dark winged moths were camouflaged against the dark background and survived.
- So natural selection favoured the dark winged moths, and their proportion in the population increased.

(iii) Human action can speed up natural selection so that evolution is seen in years instead of millions of years. Excess use of herbicides and pesticides has resulted in the selection of resistant varieties in a much shorter time scale; the same is true of microbes against which antibiotics or drugs are used, and of eukaryotic cells against drugs, where resistant organisms or cells appear in months or years, not centuries. Industrial melanism itself is an example, since the dark moths spread because of human pollution.

rows.stem:
(i) Why did Hershey and Chase use '\(^{35}\text{S}\)' and '\(^{32}\text{P}\)' in their experiment ? Explain.
(ii) State the importance of (1) blending and (2) centrifugation in their experiment.
(iii) Write the conclusion they arrived at the end of their experiment.
rows.solution:
(i) Proteins contain sulphur but no phosphorus, while DNA contains phosphorus but no sulphur. So Hershey and Chase grew some bacteriophages on a medium with radioactive phosphorus (\(^{32}\text{P}\)), which labelled their DNA, and others on radioactive sulphur (\(^{35}\text{S}\)), which labelled their protein. This let them detect whether DNA or protein passed from the virus into the bacteria.

(ii)
1. **Blending:** after infection, agitating the mixture in a blender removes the viral coats from the bacteria (E. coli).
2. **Centrifugation:** spinning in a centrifuge separates the virus particles (in the supernatant) from the heavier bacteria (in the pellet), so each can be checked for radioactivity.

(iii) Bacteria infected with viruses carrying radioactive DNA were radioactive, while those infected with viruses carrying radioactive protein were not; the radioactivity of the protein stayed in the supernatant. So DNA, not protein, enters the bacteria from the virus, and they concluded that **DNA is the genetic material** passed from virus to bacteria.
